title: Short Stuff: Papasan Chairs
summary: Short Stuff episode on papasan chairs. The hosts note they have never owned one and recommend John Kelly's Atlas Obscura research as the best source, though the chair's origin remains unsolved. They discuss the likely 1960s Philippines origin, the Pier One Imports connection (and its origins as Cost Plus, which split off and became World Market), and a 1977 MAC Flyer military magazine joke mentioning a papasan chair from Clark Air Base. They offer a theory that the name came from American GIs in Vietnam-era Southeast Asia, where "papasan" was slang for pimp, and that the chairs spread in the US in the mid-1970s. They then describe the chair's look, its variants (rattan, bamboo, moon chair, woven string or metal bases), its association with hippie culture, its midcentury modern revival, and where to buy new or used ones.

segments.title: Opening banter and no-papasan confession
segments.summary: The hosts open the show, joke about the intro, and say neither of them has owned a papasan or futon. They recommend John Kelly's Atlas Obscura research as the best source.

segments.title: Unsolved origin and Pier One connection
segments.summary: The hosts say the chair's origin and name are still unclear. They suggest the 1960s Philippines as the likely origin, and discuss Pier One's history, including its Cost Plus roots and the Tandy Corporation link.

segments.title: Vietnam-era GIs and the name theory
segments.summary: The hosts explain that the Philippines origin conflicts with the Japanese meaning of papasan. They describe a theory that American GIs in Southeast Asia brothels called the chairs papasan (slang for pimp), and cite a 1977 MAC Flyer joke that mentions a papasan chair from Clark Air Base.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: The hosts announce a break before returning to the topic.

segments.title: 1970s popularity, chair variants, and hippie associations
segments.summary: The hosts say papasan chairs became popular in the US by the mid-1970s, probably through soldiers and Pier One. They describe the classic big round cushioned bowl, variants such as moon chairs and bamboo versions, and the hippie and artsy associations. They also mention the midcentury modern revival and a Malaysian story about portrait photos.

segments.title: Where to buy papasan chairs
segments.summary: The hosts say papasan chairs can still be bought new, including at Pier One's site, which redirects from papasan dot com, and used through online classifieds. They mention prices and suggest a sturdy support for hanging versions.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts close the short episode, noting there is no listener mail, and give the show's credits.
